app.title: Swiss Influenza Monitor
app.summary: On start, the interface fetches the latest weekly case reports from a public-health API, or falls back to a stored copy, and shows which data version it is using. On the latest-status page the person chooses how many recent weeks to look back. They then see the national curve for the past year with that window marked, a tile map of the average per region, and bars by pathogen type, sex and age group. They can switch between population-normalised incidence and raw counts. On the history pages they choose an end date and a window length to map any past period, and follow each subgroup's share of incidence over time, hidden when overall incidence is too low.

task.text: Watch the current level of a notifiable infection by region and population subgroup, and set it against past seasons.

data.text: Weekly surveillance case reports with counts, incidence per 100,000 and population, broken down by region, age group, sex and pathogen type.
data.item: one ISO week's case count and incidence for one region or population subgroup

stage.text: exploring the latest published surveillance figures and putting them in the context of past waves

mechanism.text: A look-back window, set with a slider (or with an end date and a week count on the history page), drives every view at once. A full-year line chart shades the window, a zoomed line chart shows it close up, and the window's averages fill a hexagon tile map of regions and horizontal bar charts of subgroups. Further pages stack the national curve above relative-incidence area charts per subgroup, with a cutoff slider below which the shares are not drawn.

workflow.name: summarize a recent time window of regional counts against their history

steps.here: Weekly reports are downloaded from the public-health API at start-up, cached for a day, reduced to weekly case rows, and split by region, age, sex and type. The sidebar shows the data version, the download time, the reference date, and whether stored fallback data is in use.
A vertical slider sets 1 to 20 weeks back from the reference date. The window is shaded on a full-year national line chart and shown close up in a zoomed line chart.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Weekly incidence or case count is averaged per region over the window and drawn on a hexagon tile map. A radio button switches between Incid and Count, and a slider sets the upper colour threshold.
Horizontal bar charts show the window's average for pathogen type, sex and age group.

On History CNT, a date slider picks the period's end and pills pick its length in weeks. Incidence and count tile maps for that period sit side by side under a full-history line chart that shades the period.

steps.step: follow each subgroup's share over time
steps.here: On History GRP, the national incidence curve is stacked above relative-incidence area charts for age, sex and type. A cutoff slider hides the shares in weeks when overall incidence is too low to estimate them.

distinctive: Incidence normalised by population and raw case counts are kept separate and labelled so, with their own colour scales and thresholds.
Regions are drawn as equal-sized hexagons on a fixed tile layout, so small regions are as visible as large ones.
Subgroup shares are left out in weeks when overall incidence is below a cutoff the person sets, because shares are unreliable at low counts.
The look-back window is counted from a reference date and marked on the yearly curve, which shows where the current period sits in the season.
If the API fails, stored historical data is used, and the sidebar says so.
